text: The adverbial theory (Ducasse, Chisholm) analyses 'I sense a red sense-datum' as 'I am appeared to ___' - replacing the inner object with a manner or adverb of sensing.
explanation: Adverbialism reconstrues 'I sense a red sense-datum' as 'I am appeared to redly', treating the redness as a manner (adverb) of sensing rather than an inner object, thereby avoiding ontological commitment to sense-data. (Its chief difficulty is the 'many-properties problem'.) The expected word is 'redly'.
